title: Population Growth Holds Steady in Midsized Cities Amid Widespread Slowdown (Vintage 2025 city and town estimates, CB26-80)
measures: Fastest-growing cities of 20,000+ (Celina 24.6%, Fulshear 21.0%, Princeton, Melissa, Anna, Forney, Hutto, Greenville in Texas); largest numeric gains (Fort Worth +19,512 to 1,028,117; San Antonio +14,359 to 1,548,422; Houston +11,515 to 2,397,315; McKinney +8,504); 15 most populous cities (Houston 4th, San Antonio 7th, Dallas 9th at 1,329,491, Fort Worth 10th, Austin 12th at 1,002,632); Austin crossed 1 million; Harris County and Tarrant County among top five counties for housing-unit gains.
limitations: Estimates are revised each vintage; compare only within the same vintage. Covers incorporated city limits, not metro areas.

title: Slow Growth Impacts Nation’s Largest Counties Hardest (Vintage 2025 county and metro estimates, CB26-56)
geography: United States counties and metro areas
measures: Top metro numeric growth 2024–25: Houston-Pasadena-The Woodlands 1st (+126,720 to 7,904,627), Dallas-Fort Worth-Arlington 2nd (+123,557 to 8,477,157), Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos 6th (+53,796 to 2,620,945), San Antonio-New Braunfels 9th (+38,402 to 2,813,140), with April 2020 estimates bases. Top county numeric growth: Harris (+48,695), Collin (+42,966), Montgomery (+30,011), Fort Bend (+24,163), Williamson (+23,814). Waller and Kaufman counties 2nd and 3rd by percent growth (5.7%). Dallas County 2,664,013 (2024) to 2,661,397 (2025). Fastest-growing counties in large metros tended to be on the outer edges, a pattern especially pronounced in Texas; lower net international migration slowed growth nationally.
limitations: Estimates; revised annually. County and metro totals, not city or ZIP.

title: Subcounty Resident Population Estimates, Texas: April 1, 2020 to July 1, 2025 (SUB-EST2025_48)
publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program
geography: Texas incorporated places and county parts of places
measures: Estimates base 2020 and July 1 2020–2025 for each city and for the part of each city in each county: Houston 2,299,649 → 2,397,315 (Harris part 2,347,346; Fort Bend 43,668; Montgomery 6,301); Dallas 1,304,341 → 1,329,491 (Dallas County 1,245,355; Collin 54,266; Denton 29,865); Fort Worth 918,892 → 1,028,117 (Tarrant 1,006,863; Denton 19,577; Parker 1,677); Austin 958,151 → 1,002,632 (Travis 929,657; Williamson 72,071; Hays 904); San Antonio 1,433,348 → 1,548,422 (Bexar 1,548,411); Texas 29,149,498 → 31,709,821.
limitations: Estimates; county-part rows with zero population indicate land in that county with no estimated residents. Vintage 2025 supersedes earlier vintages.

title: List 1: Core Based Statistical Areas, Metropolitan Divisions and Combined Statistical Areas, July 2023

title: Texas Health Steps
publisher: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
measures: Texas Health Steps provides checkups and related services for children birth through age 20 who have Medicaid, including dental checkups starting at 6 months of age.
limitations: Member-facing program page; no enrolment counts.

title: Texas Health Steps: Dental Providers
publisher: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
measures: THSteps dental benefits are administered as Children's Medicaid Dental Services by dental managed care organizations for most clients ages 20 and younger; checkups recommended every three to six months from 6 months of age; notes TMHP benefit changes effective March 1, 2025 (teledentistry billing) and October 1, 2024 (orthodontic benefit).
limitations: Provider policy page; benefit details change through TMHP notices.

title: Compare Value-Added or Extra Services Offered by Texas CHIP Dental Services Plans (C-DECC-10/01/26)
publisher: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
measures: Lists three CHIP dental plans: DentaQuest, MCNA Dental and UnitedHealthcare Dental.
limitations: Member comparison chart of extra services; not a network or enrolment report.

title: Compare Value-Added or Extra Services Offered by Texas Children's Medicaid Dental Services Plans (M-DECC-PRD-10/01/26)
publisher: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
measures: Lists three Children's Medicaid Dental Services plans: DentaQuest, MCNA Dental and UnitedHealthcare Dental.
limitations: Member comparison chart; does not show which practices are in network.

title: 22 Tex. Admin. Code § 108.53 – Fees
publisher: Legal Information Institute (mirror of the Texas Administrative Code)
measures: Fee advertising must be clear and non-deceptive; an advertisement that includes a price must disclose the service, usually-required related services, that the fee is a minimum, the dates the price is available, the standard fee and any cash-only limit for discounts, and the basis of any fee range; prohibits representing services as free when a third-party payor including Medicaid pays.
limitations: Unofficial mirror; adopted effective May 1, 2013. Verify against the official Texas Administrative Code and consult counsel.

title: 22 Tex. Admin. Code § 108.55 – Advertising for General Dentists
publisher: Legal Information Institute (mirror of the Texas Administrative Code)
measures: A general dentist advertising specific services (example given: orthodontics, dentures, implants) must include 'General Dentist' or 'General Dentistry' directly after the dentist's name, in a font no smaller than the largest font used for the services; broadcast ads must say it audibly; service listings must not imply specialization.
limitations: Unofficial mirror; amended per 46 TexReg (September 24, 2021). Verify against the official code and consult counsel.

title: 22 Tex. Admin. Code § 108.59 – Website Disclosures
publisher: Legal Information Institute (mirror of the Texas Administrative Code)
measures: Dental practice websites should clearly disclose ownership of the website, services provided, office addresses and contact information, and licensure and qualifications of dentists and associated providers.
limitations: Unofficial mirror; adopted effective May 1, 2013. Verify against the official code.

title: Tell Google about localized versions of your page
measures: Use hreflang (HTML, headers or sitemaps) to tell Google about language variants of a page; translating only the template while main content stays in one language does not create a real language version; x-default fallback for selectors.
limitations: Page last updated 2025-12-10; describes signals, not ranking outcomes.

title: Observation: sample of five Houston dental practice homepages
measures: research/local/texas-houston-practices.md — observable homepage features (booking path, hours, languages, insurance/payment information, published prices, location content) on five practice websites found with WebSearch queries: dentist Houston TX; dental implants Houston TX; pediatric dentist Houston; Bellaire/Chinatown dentist.
limitations: Small, non-random convenience sample of homepages on one date; describes websites, not practice performance, demand or revenue. Sites that blocked automated access were skipped. Original search reference: https://www.bing.com/search?q=dentist+Houston+TX.
